previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of paraplegia, neurogenic bladder, and chronic Foley catheter use was admitted with left flank pain, cloudy urine, and nausea, diagnosed with acute pyelonephritis due to E. coli, and treated with IV meropenem followed by ceftriaxone and transitioned to oral cefpodoxime. She also presented with constipation causing abdominal pain and distension, which worsened and required NG tube decompression and manual disimpaction, with subsequent improvement on aggressive bowel regimen. Her INR was subtherapeutic for her known right leg DVT, so she was bridged with Lovenox and restarted on warfarin with outpatient monitoring arranged. Metabolic acidosis resolved with IV fluids. She was discharged to a shelter with medication adjustments, including continued warfarin, antibiotics, and enhanced bowel regimen, with close follow-up for INR and primary care.

Brief Hospital Course:
This is a ___ year old female with PMH of polysubstance abuse, 
poorly controlled DM2, spinal paralysis secondary to a gun shot 
wound, wheelchair bound with a neurogenic bladder, indwelling 
Foley, and bowel incontinence, who presented with left sided 
flank/abdominal pain for 5 days likely secondary to 
constipation, med non-compliance, and recent drug use. 
.
#. Abdominal pain- It seems as though the patient has had 
multiple admissions for left flank pain which has been 
attributed to pyelonephritis in the past.  Of note, she did not 
have any evidence of pyelonephritis on CT imaging from ___ when 
she was also admitted for left flank pain.  She remained 
afebrile, normotensive with BP=130s/80s, UA was benign for a 
patient with a chronic indwelling Foley, and she did not have a 
leukocytosis.  Urine culture returned positive for >100,000 GNRs 
which was considered to be colonization given her chronic Foley. 
 Of note, she reports that her Foley was changed out last week.  
As a result, she was not started on any antibiotics.  She has 
been non-compliant with her home medications and had a tox 
screen positive for cocaine, amphetamines, and tricyclics.  Her 
pain seems chronic in nature and may be secondary to underlying 
constipation as she noted some improvement in her symptoms after 
a bowel movement.  She also reported an episode of BRBPR which 
may have been secondary to vasoconstriction and ischemia from 
cocaine use.  Her pain was treated with Maalox/lidocaine PRN, 
Toradol PRN, and acetaminophen (<2 grams) PRN which all seemed 
to improve her symptoms per her report. 
.
#. Anemia- The patient's hematocrit was in the mid ___ which was 
slightly up from her recent baseline.  It was suspected that she 
was mildly hypovolemic and was started on IVFs.
.
#. Polysubstance abuse- She has a h/o heavy EtOH use and had a 
tox screen positive for TCAs, amphetamines, and cocaine.  There 
was a low likelihood of overdose on tricyclics.  The patient 
denied taking any of her prescribed meds for multiple days and 
she did not have any typical findings of TCA overdose on her 
EKG.  She was monitored on telemetry with no events noted.  Her 
amitriptyline was discontinued on discharge.
.  
#. h/o R leg paresis and L foot paresis- No active issues.  She 
was continued on her home neurontin, but her home amitriptyline 
was discontinued given initial concern for overdose. 
.  
#. Depression- Continued home fluoxetine.  She denied current 
SI/HI.  
.  
#. Diabetes Mellitus, type II- Her last A1C was 6.5% in ___.  
She is on metformin, but has poor med compliance.  She was 
maintained on HISS with QID finger sticks and transitioned back 
to metformin upon discharge.
.

likely contribution from drugs as patient is positive for 
cocaine and amphetamines.  She had a normal INR and creatinine.
